paper_title: Prometheus 2 An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating   Other Language Models
caption: When merging models, the influence of relative evaluation on absolute evaluation is greater than the influence of absolute evaluation on relative evaluation. Performance of Direct Assessment (colored in green) and Pairwise Ranking (colored in blue) when altering the value to merge evaluator LMs trained on different formats.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of Direct Assessment (green line), Pairwise Ranking (blue line), and Average Performance (black line) across varying merging ratios of evaluator language models trained on different formats. The x-axis represents the "Direct Assessment : Pairwise Ranking Merging Ratio," ranging from 1:9 to 9:1, indicating the proportion of models trained on direct assessment versus pairwise ranking. The left y-axis measures "Direct Assessment Pearson Correlation" on a scale from 0.500 to 0.675, while the right y-axis measures "Pairwise Ranking Accuracy" on a scale from 50 to 80. The green line for Direct Assessment starts at a correlation of approximately 0.495 at a 1:9 ratio, increases sharply to a peak of about 0.670 at a 5:5 ratio, and then declines to around 0.590 at a 9:1 ratio. The blue line for Pairwise Ranking begins at a high accuracy of about 80 at a 1:9 ratio, decreases steadily to approximately 50 at a 9:1 ratio, with a notable drop occurring around the 7:3 to 8:2 ratios. The black line for Average Performance shows a more gradual increase from around 0.575 at 1:9 to a peak of about 0.625 at a 5:5 ratio, followed by a decline to approximately 0.555 at a 9:1 ratio. The data suggests that the influence of relative evaluation (Pairwise Ranking) on absolute evaluation (Direct Assessment) is more pronounced than the reverse, as indicated by the stronger correlation and accuracy trends in the green and blue lines, respectively.
